questions.explanation: The passive reporting structure 'is said to' + infinitive reports rumour formally.
questions.q: He ___ last week, according to the press.

options: He was understood to have known the risks all along.
He was understood that he knew the risks all along.
He was understood to know the risks all along.
He understood to have known the risks all along.
questions.explanation: 'Was understood to' + perfect infinitive reports a past belief about an earlier event.
Backshift turns 'will' into 'would' in reported speech about the future.
questions.q: She said she ___ call back later.

questions.explanation: The perfect infinitive 'to have been' reports a past state viewed from the past.
A past reporting verb backshifts present perfect to past perfect.
questions.q: He told me he ___ when I arrived.

options: The parties are reported that they negotiate a settlement.
The parties are reported to have negotiated a settlement.
The parties are reported to be negotiating a settlement.
The parties report to be negotiating a settlement.
questions.explanation: 'Are reported to be' + present infinitive reports a current situation.
'Denied' + gerund is the correct pattern; 'denied to' is ungrammatical.
The continuous infinitive 'to be lying' reports an ongoing past rumour.
Only the backshifted version correctly reports the original present-tense question.
options: He asked where I was going
He asked where was I going
He asked where I am going
He asked me where did I go
He was thought that he wrote the anonymous letters.
He was thought to write the anonymous letters.
He was thought to have written the anonymous letters.
He thought to have written the anonymous letters.
questions.explanation: 'Was thought to have' + past participle reports a past belief about a completed act.
'Accused of' + gerund is the fixed pattern for reported accusations.
The reporting is in the past, so the original 'am' backshifts to 'was'.
'Admitted' takes a gerund in reported confessions.

options: The company is expected that it announces record profits by June.
The company is expected to announce record profits by June.
The company is expected to have announced record profits by June.
The company expects to have announced record profits by June.
questions.explanation: 'Is expected to' + perfect infinitive reports an anticipated completed action.
'Warned against' + gerund reports the warning correctly.
Backshift moves 'can' to 'could' when the reporting verb is past.
The infinitive 'to be' reports the current alleged state; the perfect would imply completion.
'Claimed' + perfect infinitive reports a past achievement claim.
The reported imperative uses 'told' + object + not + infinitive.
Only the fully backshifted version keeps tenses consistent in formal reported speech.
options: She said she had been waiting since dawn
She said she has been waiting since dawn
She said she was waiting since dawn
She said she had waited since dawn yesterday
